newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: COAL MINERS IN AUSTRALIA'S NSW TO STAY AT WORK.
newsitem.headline: COAL MINERS IN AUSTRALIA'S NSW TO STAY AT WORK.

text.p: Members of the Construction, Forestry Mining and Energy Union (CFMEU) on Wednesday voted to accept a leadership recommendation that they stay on the job at the Hunter Valley No 1 coal mine, north of Sydney.
The mine, owned by Coal and Allied Industries Ltd (CAIL), which is turn is about 70 percent owned by Rio Tinto Ltd, was subject to a six-week strike which lasted until July 22.

Miners then entered into a 21-day negotiating period with CAIL. On expiry of this period, with no resolution reached between the union and CAIL, the Australian Industrial Relations Commission on Tuesday recommended that the union and the company continue to negotiate for a further 21 days.
Acceptance by CFMEU members of the union recommendation means the mine will not be subject to immediate strike action.

The mine, which produces 25,000 tonnes of semi-soft coking coal and thermal coal a day, exports to Japan and other buyers in east Asia. One million tonnes of production was disrupted in the last strike.
